project.name: NAR Telegram trading pool
project.purpose: A Telegram Mini App and bot for a private group to deposit stablecoins into deterministic per-user vaults, receive pooled manual trading returns, and request manual withdrawals.
project.status: initial backend prototype implemented; product workflow remains in design and alignment work.
project.maintenance: Update this file only when the user explicitly asks for an update.

scope.valuation: All supported stablecoins are accounted as 1 USD for now. A depeg is handled manually during withdrawal.

identity_and_vaults.telegram_identity: The backend validates Telegram Mini App initData and maps Telegram's stable numeric user ID to an internal user ID. Do not use initDataUnsafe as a trusted identity source.
identity_and_vaults.vault_model: Each user has deterministic Vault contracts deployed by the Factory. A user may have multiple vaults through a per-user nonce.
identity_and_vaults.salt: Derive the CREATE2 salt from internalUserId and vaultNonce; do not expose or rely directly on the Telegram user ID.
identity_and_vaults.cross_chain_address_requirement: The Factory address, Vault creation bytecode, and salt must match across chains for a user's vault address to match across chains. Token choice must not affect the vault address.
identity_and_vaults.deposit_method: Users send ERC-20 tokens directly to a displayed vault address or QR code. They do not call a vault deposit function.

control.factory_owner: Separate multisig; deploys vaults and manually sweeps vault tokens.
control.proxy_admin: A different multisig; controls Factory upgrades.
control.treasury: No onchain configured treasury. The factory owner supplies the destination for each manual sweep.

contracts.vault_behavior: Vaults accept direct ERC-20 transfers. Only the Factory can transfer ERC-20 or native balances out.
known_contract_decisions: Zero salt deployment was fixed by the user.
Vaults are persistent; selfdestruct is not part of this design.
The backend credits only configured token-contract addresses per chain; unapproved tokens sent to a vault are not credited.
Contracts remain unchanged for now; sweep events and recipient-address checks are deferred hardening work.

flow: User selects chain, token, intended amount, and lock tier in the Mini App.
The Mini App shows the user's vault address and QR code.
User transfers a stablecoin directly to the vault and confirms they sent it.
Backend scans the known vault for configured-token transfer events; if it cannot match one, it asks the user for the transaction hash.
The transfer remains pending until the operator sweeps and confirms the amount.
A successful sweep activates the position.
deposit_lifecycle.deposit_identity: Use chainId + transactionHash + logIndex. A transaction can contain multiple relevant token transfers.
deposit_lifecycle.confirmation_policy: No fixed block-confirmation delay. A transfer is pending until the manual sweep succeeds; an unavailable or reorganized transfer cannot become active.
deposit_lifecycle.earning_start: A position begins earning and its lock begins only when the sweep/confirmation succeeds. The source transfer timestamp is retained as evidence only.
deposit_lifecycle.intent_expiry: Deposit intents expire after 24 hours. They snapshot the exact selected chain and whitelisted token contract address.
deposit_lifecycle.minimum_and_topups: The minimum is 50 USD. A below-minimum intent can accumulate multiple verified transfers of the same configured token on the same chain until it reaches the minimum.
deposit_lifecycle.counterfactual_vaults: The user may receive and send to a deterministic counterfactual vault address before the vault is deployed. The admin deploys the vault through the multisig before sweeping and confirming it.
deposit_lifecycle.unmatched_transfers: A supported incoming transfer without an intent enters manual matching; it is never auto-credited.
deposit_lifecycle.amount_mismatch: When received amount differs from intent, the user must approve the confirmed actual amount before activation. The UI warns that an incorrect amount may lead to loss of funds.
deposit_lifecycle.token_warning: The app displays the exact accepted token-contract address. Other tokens are not credited and may be unrecoverable.

portfolio_model.per_user: Each Telegram user has exactly one combined portfolio in one pooled strategy.
portfolio_model.chains_and_vaults: Chains, vaults, and stablecoins are deposit and withdrawal routes only; they do not create separate user portfolios.

positions_and_locks.meaning: Rates are projected, compounded APYs. They are not guaranteed: actual historical return may be lower or higher. The default positive-P&L allocation targets each tier's projected APY; the operator may grant a one-time higher bonus funded from manager excess profit.
positions_and_locks.lots: Every confirmed deposit or relock allocation creates an independent position lot. A user can hold multiple lots in different tiers and split a deposit or relock among them. Adding money to an active lock starts a new full-duration lot.
positions_and_locks.maturity: At lock expiry, the lot moves to the liquid pool at its current value. Locks never renew automatically.
positions_and_locks.relocking: A user can relock any available amount, including gains, into one or more new lots. Max selects all available value. An active lock can only be extended to a longer tier; it becomes a new lot with a new start and maturity time and no fee.

multi_pool_accounting.ledger_location: Backend only; contracts do not calculate balances or yield.
multi_pool_accounting.pools: Maintain five USD NAV/share pools: liquid, 1-month, 2-month, 3-month, and manager. A user holds shares through their position lots; the manager pool is visible only to the admin.
multi_pool_accounting.operator_input: For each settlement, the operator enters the current total USD value of all managed funds, including the manager pool and accumulated early-withdrawal fees. Server time is the settlement time; it cannot be backdated.
multi_pool_accounting.positive_pnl: First credit participant pools toward their compounded projected APY for the elapsed settlement interval, with time-weighting when a lock matures during that interval. The manager pool receives all remaining positive value. The operator may move part of that manager excess to selected lots as a one-time bonus; it is not a persistent rate change.
multi_pool_accounting.negative_pnl: When reported total NAV falls, reduce every pool, including the manager pool, by the same percentage of its current NAV. There is no loss carryforward or high-water mark.
multi_pool_accounting.settlement_order: Settle the pool before every balance-changing action: deposit confirmation, withdrawal reservation or payment, relock, and maturity conversion.
multi_pool_accounting.compounding: Projected rates compound. For an elapsed period, calculate the tier cap as (1 + projectedAPY)^(days/365) - 1.
invariants: After settlement, the sum of the five pool NAVs equals the reported total NAV.
Pool share prices change with settlement; deposits, withdrawals, relocks, maturity transfers, and position bonuses mint or burn shares at the applicable current price.
All USD values and shares use fixed-point integers; never floating-point arithmetic.

withdrawals.processing: Users submit requests in the Mini App; the operator manually swaps, bridges, and sends the requested stablecoin on the requested supported chain.
withdrawals.early_locked_withdrawal: For the selected amount taken from an active lock, charge 10% of its current value. For example, withdrawing 400 USD pays 360 USD and credits 40 USD to the manager pool. The quote must clearly show this fee before approval.
withdrawals.partial_withdrawal: Allowed. Burn the shares for the selected current value; the remaining lot stays active with its remaining shares and original maturity.
withdrawals.mature_or_liquid_withdrawal: No early-withdrawal fee; current pool value can be withdrawn.
withdrawals.payout_address: Users enter any valid EVM payout address for each request after selecting a supported chain, stablecoin, and amount. Previously used payout addresses are saved per user and can be selected for convenience.
withdrawals.reservation: On explicit user approval, a withdrawal request reserves the requested amount so it cannot be relocked or requested twice. The user can cancel only while the request is pending.
withdrawals.request_quote: For any active-lock amount, show the affected position, 10% early-withdrawal fee, and final payout before user approval. The result is fixed when approved.
withdrawals.liquidity_order: Use liquid balance first; the user chooses any locked positions and amounts needed for the remainder.
withdrawals.admin_outcome: Admin may reject a request with a user-visible reason. Mark paid only after the outgoing transaction hash is recorded.
withdrawals.network_fees: Admin absorbs withdrawal network fees for now.
withdrawals.history: Record requested payout chain, token, amount, payout address, status, operator decision, early-withdrawal fee, and outgoing transaction hash.

mini_app.performance_rules: Show each user only their projected APY and historical APY, calculated from retained balance history while adjusting for deposits, withdrawals, relocks, and maturity changes. Historical APY may be negative. Gross pool performance and manager excess are admin-only.
mini_app.landing: Show the 6-10% projected APY range and illustrative projections such as a 1,000 USD balance over one year. State that actual returns may be lower or higher based on trading performance and market conditions.
mini_app.relocking: Locks never renew automatically; users choose every new lock manually.

authentication.user_access: No separate login screen. The Mini App sends Telegram initData to the backend, which validates its signature and uses the verified Telegram user ID to load only that user’s records.
authentication.admin_access: The separate browser dashboard uses Telegram Login with the bot OpenID Connect flow. The backend validates the Telegram ID token and permits access only when its Telegram user ID is on the admin allowlist. Initially, the allowlist contains only the owner account.
authentication.client_trust_boundary: Never trust a Telegram ID supplied by the client outside validated Telegram initData.

admin_dashboard.surface: Separate browser-based dashboard for laptop use.
functions: manage supported assets and user records
generate Factory deployment and sweep calldata for manual Safe submission
admin_dashboard.authentication: Telegram Login OpenID Connect. Register the dashboard origin and callback URL in BotFather; validate ID-token signature, issuer, audience, expiration, nonce, and the Telegram user-ID allowlist server-side.

backend_initial_implementation.stack: Fastify, TypeScript, Drizzle ORM, PostgreSQL, Zod, and pg.
implemented: A development-only admin deposit-confirmation endpoint at POST /admin/deposits/confirm.
Core users, admins, chains, assets, vaults, pooled state, positions, deposits, withdrawals, ledger, idempotency, and audit-log tables.
Transactional deposit confirmation that mints pooled shares, writes balanced USD ledger entries, updates a user position and pooled state, and writes an audit record.
Input validation for IDs, whole-unit token amounts, transaction hashes, transfer indexes, active user/vault/asset relationships, and USDT/USDC/DAI symbols.
backend_initial_implementation.verification: npm run build completed successfully on 2026-10-19.
backend_initial_implementation.current_model: One USD-denominated pooled NAV/share prototype. It must be replaced with five pool states and per-lot position shares: liquid, 1-month, 2-month, 3-month, and manager.
required_alignment: Replace development-only environment-variable admin identity with Telegram Mini App and Telegram Login authentication.
Add deposit intents, 24-hour expiry, pending/manual matching, amount-change approval, vault deployment, sweep, and confirmation states.
Verify onchain ERC-20 transfers before crediting deposits; the current endpoint trusts submitted amount and transaction metadata.
